content.text:
I made one change to `0.html`: a fix for a layout bug that would push a modal dialog or popover to the bottom of the screen. It is untested in a browser, because the headless Chrome check I tried to run was blocked by this session's permissions.

## The fix

At `0.html:160`, the rule that strips the bottom margin from the last child of `body`, `main`, `li` and similar containers also matched `<dialog>` and `[popover]` elements. Both rely on the browser's `margin: auto` to centre themselves. A modal placed at the end of `<body>`, which is the usual spot, would lose its bottom margin and sit against the bottom of the viewport instead of the centre.

The selector now excludes them:

```css
:is(body, main, …, [popover]) > :last-child:where(:not(dialog, [popover])) {
  margin-block-end: 0;
}
```

The `:where()` wrapper keeps the rule's specificity the same as before, so nothing else in the cascade shifts.

## What I left alone

I went through the rest of the stylesheet and found nothing else worth changing.

Two trade-offs I did not change:

- **Scrollable tables:** `table { display: block }` lets wide tables scroll without a wrapper element, but it can drop table semantics for screen readers in older Safari. The alternative is a wrapper `<div>` around each table.
- **Trailing `<script>` or `<template>`:** if one of these is the last child of `<body>`, the last visible element keeps its 1rem bottom margin. It only adds a little extra space at the bottom of the page.

The page content is still just a title and an `<h1>` of "0". If "improve" meant the content or the visual design rather than the base stylesheet, tell me which and I'll work on that.
